title: Prospective observational study investigating metabolism-related changes in the ocular fundus in individuals with obesity during weight loss.
summary:
This study is a planned observational study that will include a total of 90 participants with obesity (defined as a body mass index [BMI] of 30 kg/m² or higher).

The aim of this study is to investigate whether weight reduction achieved through different treatment approaches – such as a lifestyle program including nutritional counseling, physical activity, and behavioral therapy, medication-assisted weight loss, or bariatric surgery (e.g., sleeve gastrectomy or gastric bypass) – has positive effects on changes in the eye. In particular, the study will examine whether weight loss can improve early changes in the small blood vessels of the retina and signs of metabolic changes within the retina.
Participants with obesity who are seeking weight reduction as part of the Obesity Outpatient Clinic at the University Hospital Schleswig-Holstein (UKSH), Campus Lübeck, will undergo regular examinations over a period of two years. Every three months, different painless and non-invasive examinations of the back of the eye will be performed. These include imaging of the retina and its blood vessels using specialized techniques (OCT-A) to detect changes in the small retinal vessels. In addition, another examination method (FLIO) will be used to assess metabolic changes in the retina.
Blood samples will also be collected at regular intervals. These samples will be analyzed, among other things, to examine specific small molecules involved in gene regulation (so-called microRNAs). These molecules may provide information about how metabolic changes in the body are affected by weight reduction.
The purpose of these examinations is to improve our understanding of how weight loss influences eye health and metabolic processes in the body.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Participants with obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m²)
- Age ≥18 years
- Initiation of one of the following weight reduction therapies within 30 days after study inclusion:
- Bariatric surgery (sleeve gastrectomy or Roux-en-Y gastric bypass)
- Pharmacological weight reduction therapy (GLP-1 receptor agonists [GLP-1 RAs])
- Conservative weight reduction measures (nutritional counseling, behavioral therapy, and exercise therapy)
Exclusion criteria:
- BMI <30 kg/m²
- Weight fluctuations of ±10% within the last 90 days
- Diabetes mellitus defined as:
- Pre-existing diagnosis of diabetes mellitus in the medical history, or
- Laboratory parameters meeting the diagnostic criteria for diabetes mellitus (at least two of the following):
- HbA1c ≥6.5%
- Fasting plasma glucose (FPG) ≥126 mg/dL
- 2-hour plasma glucose (2h-PG) ≥200 mg/dL during oral glucose tolerance testing
- Existing weight reduction therapy (e.g., GLP-1 receptor agonists [GLP-1 RAs] or GLP-1/GIP receptor agonists [GLP-1/GIP-RAs]) or initiation of such therapy within <90 days before the start of the study
- Previous bariatric surgery for weight reduction (planned surgery is not an exclusion criterion)
e.g., gastric bypass
- Psychiatric comorbidities that may interfere with adherence to the study protocol:
- Anxiety disorders
- Severe alcohol or substance abuse
Ocular conditions:
- Retinal diseases
- Glaucoma
- Diseases affecting the optic nerve
- Narrow anterior chamber angle
- High myopia (<−7.0 diopters) or high hyperopia (>+7.0 diopters) based on spherical equivalent
- Relevant media opacities
- Cataracts for which surgery is planned within the next 12 months
- Active or planned pregnancy
- Participants taking retinotoxic medications (e.g., tamoxifen, hydroxychloroquine)
- Participants expected to be unable to cooperate adequately during ocular fundus examinations (e.g., due to tremor or cognitive impairment)
- Chronic diseases for which corticosteroid pulse therapy may become necessary during the study period
- Participation in other clinical studies or treatment with investigational medicinal products within the previous 90 days
- Active malignancy within the previous 5 years
- Advanced renal impairment (eGFR <20 mL/min)
- Severe liver disease (liver cirrhosis or significant hepatic dysfunction)
- Recurrent hypertensive crises
